data.keyword: What's the best password manager for a small team?

result.keyword: What's the best password manager for a small team?
result.markdown:
For most small teams, I'd recommend **1Password or Bitwarden**\.

- **1Password** is the best all-round choice if you prioritise ease of use, security and straightforward team management.
- **Bitwarden** is the best choice if you want strong security and team-sharing features at a lower price.

The key is to choose a proper business plan, rather than having employees share personal password-manager accounts.

## My top 4 recommendations

![1Password 8.12 - TidBITS](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/34HDvvYhqgd6AnMFmrlTm3hAXFxcbeGEwY_LB_XZ_XGVtrk4a2QxTEX-2LBZt2GGXhIIaKEolAWfkyjqt2bzeCs60tKyMvcGjArpm-vdyy1ZPxujq2f9_l2uItYJrXcwCcU9bPBSy8AGv_Ou2YF6Ce5xYeilxXBZ8f7ED4T1F4V2OwIPdBn46M8zBrxXTO4w?purpose=fullsize)

**1\. 1Password**

(Best overall)

- Excellent, intuitive user experience.
- Separate vaults for departments and projects.
- Granular access permissions.
- Security alerts and password health monitoring.
- Great for non-technical employees.

**Price\:** \$24.95/month for up to 10 users, billed annually (USD).

[Official pricing](https://1password.com/pricing/business?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

---

![Free High-Quality Bitwarden Logo for Creative Design](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/p0IJzf2NCUQ2t02rqtPWDpe7Tx4YGCRNleASv1NjpztaDI--7OD-0zWJhdBi_4Wn4-v0Hr3hoS6JA2KXHdCOlvvdfHelZm6tTBmFuxgAbBftLkdqobRCpEkp4ysyI4Rm6vafJPMfHi8ri9Tdeng_QKXRw7C7a5ESA6hn8XLhRMLnvM7oFmwZESsO4_SFLJaX?purpose=fullsize)

**2\. Bitwarden**

(Best value)

- Open-source foundations.
- Shared collections and team vaults.
- Admin controls and audit logs.
- Directory synchronisation.
- Self-hosting options.

**Price\:** Teams around \$4/user/month, billed annually.

[Plan comparison](https://toolsandthrive.com/best-password-manager-for-small-business/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

---

![Keeper Security Logo PNG,  Vector (AI, EPS, CDR, PDF, SVG) - iconLogoVector](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/hjZLLtGaZjkKvsDiCoIrNA749yx3vMYIFoRmmV0blB-pAj7O30nu3RJOVVhVRwgAOkJUfJ3datZ7pfH1wp7yeplrEL3FQ-HNOpCzlVOW0OcMr1CFjIFAx50apRkdH6sYOH31WcP6gfXOxeAN8qubYhHhGYA5yXp1bc7wqtCxjN2WEQuyMALTG1Pwne14BXyG?purpose=fullsize)

**3\. Keeper**

- Strong administrative controls.
- Shared folders and delegated administration.
- Useful for regulated businesses.
- Additional security products available.

**Price\:** Business plans vary; Starter is aimed at 5–10 users.

[Plan comparison](https://www.softwarecompare.net/comparison/best-password-manager-for-business?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

---

![The best password managers in 2025 | Tom's Guide](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/S30I88layvxbkaDwXaWP5XnJ7U511ARCXJEcDjYd8i8QoMbXMBiKKYXroCriJ7kBR0oi7lM-NLlyOXMHqaLP4YKGj6rWlLsTvfSS4pKj24h_up7wZjWKu6xYF8rT-_7bc8XbvU4PlaIDiwcj88cnT8GVhbZrDMRuBptQttvTl2oiFqpoAxV9-pe3un--FrSZ?purpose=fullsize)

**4\. Proton Pass**

- Privacy-focused approach.
- Secure sharing.
- Email aliases.
- Good option for European businesses.

**Price\:** Business plans start around \$1.99/user/month, depending on tier and billing.

[Business comparison](https://technovapartners.com/en/insights/best-business-password-managers-2026?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## What I'd choose

| Your priority | My choice |
|--------|--------|
| Best overall experience | 1Password |
| Best value for money | Bitwarden |
| Strong administrative controls | Keeper |
| Privacy-focused European option | Proton Pass |


## What matters most for a small team

Whichever you choose, make sure it supports\:

1. **Shared vaults** – share company credentials without sending passwords over Slack or email.
2. **Individual accounts** – everyone has their own login.
3. **Access management** – remove someone's access immediately when they leave.
4. **Two-factor authentication** – protect every employee account.
5. **Audit logs** – understand who accessed or changed shared credentials.
6. **Role-based permissions** – employees only see the credentials they need.

## A couple of questions to narrow it down

I can make a more definitive recommendation if I know two things\:

**1\. How many people are in your team?**
